outcome: Produce a construction model and layered reference package that matches the preferred grayscale quality and later scoped directions, then obtain Nick approval.
authorizedScope: Continue modeling, render/compare/audit loops and export preparation. Subscription generation only. No final art approval by agents; no production rigging, animation, lore or game changes.

criteria.expectation: A complete creature with consistently developed large and medium forms. Review the whole body and regional closeups together before presentation.
criteria.assessment: A smooth mannequin body, sparse chunky head decoration and simple tail lobes do not share one coherent level of sculptural development. Recognizable ears and three tails are insufficient.

criteria.expectation: Reconstruct forehead, temples, cheeks and jaw as related volumes. Front and profile must retain a rounded, appealing head without copying the generated study's inward gaze.
criteria.assessment: The face narrows into a pointed lower wedge; the forehead is broad and flat, with small blunt crown spikes. The head lacks the soft cheek and cranial fullness of the head study.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the accepted large eyes while modeling curved eye volumes, surrounding lids and their transition into the skull. Match contour, relative white area and projection before adding gloss.
criteria.assessment: Tall, very regular white ovals dominate the face. Thin dark borders and projecting white rims make them read like applied plates, particularly in PROFILE.

criteria.expectation: Keep forward gaze. Separate geometric integration from later glossy material and catchlight treatment; neither can substitute for the other.
criteria.assessment: Centered dark ovals avoid the obvious inward gaze, but their flat dark treatment removes the depth and expression of the accepted eyes.

criteria.expectation: Establish the shallow paired muzzle and chin in actual geometry. Readable projection is required in profile without enlarging it into a different animal's snout.
criteria.assessment: The muzzle is barely expressed. A tiny nose and thin drawn smile sit on a nearly continuous face surface. The head study has two soft muzzle masses, a meaningful nose-to-mouth transition and chin volume.

criteria.expectation: Form connected cheek and crown masses that change the silhouette naturally. Broad flow belongs to construction; individual hair strands can wait.
criteria.assessment: Small triangular perimeter spikes are detached in visual character from the large ear locks. They do not establish the layered cheek flow visible in the references.

criteria.expectation: Establish a continuous shaggy envelope with varied overlap, width, curvature and taper. Adding more copies of the same lobe will not resolve the material or silhouette.
criteria.assessment: Sparse thick, rounded leaf or finger shapes form a repeated fringe. Long upper clumps and blunt lower clumps read as separate decorative pieces rather than shaggy coat.

criteria.expectation: A legible cupped tissue surface with soft, intentional rim transitions and coat rooted around it. A recess being opaque does not make its shape acceptable.
criteria.assessment: Dark angular recesses interrupt the inner ear. The transition from smooth tissue to the bulky rim is abrupt and mechanical.

criteria.region: Ear depth, rear surfaces and roots
criteria.expectation: Solve ear thickness, rear coat volume and cranial attachment together in front, profile and rear oblique views. Removing a mesh seam is not the same as achieving a convincing attachment.
criteria.assessment: Side views show a thin stacked assembly. Rear views show large bare cushion-like shells, with remaining root boundaries visible as curved rims. The front fringe and rear shell feel like different constructions.

criteria.expectation: Related neck, shoulder and upper-arm volumes with plausible soft transitions. The reference pose differs, so reproduce the mass relationships rather than tracing its arm outline.
criteria.assessment: A narrow smooth neck stem expands abruptly beneath the jaw and into the shoulder area. The upper torso reads as a cap with tubular arms attached.

criteria.expectation: Continuous large planes and volume transitions through chest, waist and pelvis, without circumferential bands. Check oblique light and profile, not only a front silhouette.
criteria.assessment: Horizontal shelf-like changes remain across the chest and waist. The abdomen and pelvic transition resemble stacked sections, not continuous anatomy.

criteria.expectation: Express upper-arm/forearm mass, elbow direction and wrist-to-paw transition while preserving compact animal extremities. Lowered arms should expose these forms, not excuse them.
criteria.assessment: Upper arms and forearms are largely uniform curved tubes, with weak elbow structure. Wrists narrow into mitten-like ends without a convincing change of plane or articulation.

criteria.expectation: Rebuild the paw's outer volume and digit grouping before claw detail. Show front, side and underside as needed; retain the absence of a human thumb.
criteria.assessment: The forepaw is a flat-ended mitten with evenly repeated rounded digit bumps and small nail-like additions. The reference has a fuller tapered paw, grouped digits and claws emerging from them.

criteria.expectation: Integrate the extra bounding strength into hip/thigh/knee form. Modest fullness must not become a literal rabbit leg or isolated muscle balloon.
criteria.assessment: Added thigh fullness reads as oval swelling. The knee region has abrupt bands and pinches instead of a coherent transition between upper and lower leg.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the straight joint-to-joint shin while shaping its surrounding volume and calf taper. Judge the rendered contour and planes, not only the numerical centerline.
criteria.assessment: Lower-leg contours remain simplified, with changes of direction and thickness that read as flexible tubes. Straight control points did not establish convincing surface anatomy.

criteria.expectation: Restore local joint structure, a believable change of direction and the reference's sloping paw roof. Avoid both a human heel and a featureless continuous arc.
criteria.assessment: ANKLE / PAW PROFILE still shows a long rubbery bend sweeping into a toe bulb. There is no sufficiently clear ankle transition or supported foot volume.

criteria.expectation: Build a substantial paw body behind the digits, integrated toes and clear ground contact. Toe bumps and claws cannot stand in for the entire foot.
criteria.assessment: Small repeated toe lobes sit at the end of a thin foot. The whole-body render looks under-supported compared with the broad compact paws in the accepted study.

criteria.expectation: Retain three full tails and pointed ends while refining their three-dimensional cross-sections, curvature and taper. Do not rotate each tail for each camera to imitate incompatible generated views.
criteria.assessment: The three tails remain simple crescent or leaf-like lobes with a repeated construction. Their sectional fullness and tip transitions are less developed than the accepted smooth rear study. Profile occlusion produces compressed lobes that need geometric assessment.

criteria.expectation: Preserve the centered, body-level three-way fusion with no stalk or extra bulb; refine continuity into a restrained pelvis. Occlusion alone is not evidence that the root moved to the left.
criteria.assessment: The modeled root looks pinched and creased where the large lobes converge. Rear shading still leaves a prominent rounded haunch beside it. A common central coordinate does not establish the accepted visual transition.

criteria.expectation: Develop controlled medium-scale planes and attachments. More triangles, global smoothing or fur cannot replace this work.
criteria.assessment: Large areas are featureless while a few boundaries are overemphasized. Smoothing joins shapes but erases useful plane changes and leaves other transitions visibly banded.

audit.comparison: Candidate 0020 fails reference quality across large and medium forms. Full audit and actual reference images are bound above.
audit.regressions: Preserve accepted central body-level three-tail fusion, forward gaze and animal-paw direction while fixing modeled equivalents.
audit.scopeCheck: Audit findings remain authorized implementation work. The new completion-system request does not mark Akinza complete.
